headline: The AI trade got a defibrillator from CoreWeave — NDX +2.3%, VIX -10.1% — but it was bought with the bond market shut, a dollar at the 100th percentile and gold cracking $4,000.
summary: Yesterday the relief was offshore only; today it reached US cash, and hard. SPX +1.3% to 7,619.4, NDX +2.3% to 28,374 and flipping to turning_up, RUT +0.9%, DJT +1.2%. VIX -10.1% to 17.49, VIX3M -6.8% to 19.24, term structure back to 0.909. Credit confirmed: HY OAS -8bp to 3.34, CCC -6bp to 13.11, BBB -3bp to 1.13, IG -2bp to 0.91, HYG/IEF +0.4% and turning up, BKLN at the 97th percentile. Asia extended it overnight — TAIEX +2.9% (+5.8% on the week), KOSPI +2.5%, Nikkei +1.5%. The risk regime improved to -10 from -15. The catalyst was a single beat-and-raise in AI infrastructure, and the rally happened with the Treasury market closed for Veterans Day — the rates series are still stamped 9-10 Nov. That is a bounce that has not yet been priced by the asset class that caused the drawdown.

Because the dollar never blinked. DXY +0.6% to 102.83 — the 100th percentile of its 52-week range, +1.3% on the week — with EURUSD -0.6% to 1.1098 at the 0th percentile, USDCHF +0.9%, GBPUSD -0.5%, USDCAD 1.4249 at the 96th percentile and USDJPY grinding to 159.62. The dollar composite is -22, rates -33. The fracture is no longer generic EM: USDBRL +1.3% to 5.5827 with a 1-month z of 3.44 and acceleration +2.79, EWZ -26.2% on the month with acceleration -3.47, Bovespa -17.7% at z=-3.45 — while Mexico sits at the opposite pole, IPC at the 100th percentile and EWW +7.6% on the month. Asia FX stays the carry-friendly side: USDKRW -0.4%, USDCNY at the 3rd percentile, USDINR z=-2.85.

The new damage today is in metals. Gold 4,004.4, -0.6% and -4.4% on the month at the 7th percentile of its year, 10.9% below its 200-day; GLD -2.7%; the miners snapped after their week-long squeeze, GDX -5.4%, GDXJ -6.0%, NEM -4.2%. Silver at the 4th percentile and 25.5% below its 200-day, platinum at the 8th. A 10-year real yield of 2.66 sitting 19% above its 200-day plus a record-percentile dollar is the mechanism; this is a real-rate squeeze, not a growth signal. The other non-participant is the AI electron chain: on a +1.3% tape GEV -3.9%, CEG -3.0%, NLR -3.6%, URA -3.5%, REMX -3.5%, with VST -18.8%, GEV -20.6% and GRID -11.9% on the month. The chips bounced; the power that feeds them did not. Energy also stayed soft — Brent -13.8% and gasoline -22.5% on the month at z=-2.07.

Positioning remains the dominant fact and both tails are three sigma. Growth/value z=-3.24 at the 4th percentile, high-beta/low-vol -19.9% on the month at z=-3.09, MTUM z=-3.03, SMH/SPY z=-2.74, QQQ/SPY at the 16th percentile — against RSP/SPY at z=3.75 with acceleration +3.39, MCD z=3.83 (+20.0% on the month), HD z=2.84 (+20.7%), XLV z=2.47 at the 98th percentile, SPLV z=2.33, KIE at the 97th. There is no recession under this unwind: claims 189k at the 0th percentile, unemployment 4.1%, JOLTS 7,523 and +4.6%, growth pulse +11. The live mispricing is inflation — Tuesday's selloff came from a hot print, core CPI is turning up at z=0.93 with the index at the 100th percentile and the inflation composite has rebounded to +27 from +13, yet 10-year breakevens are 2.20 at the 6th percentile and 2s10s is 25bp at the 9th. Bear flattening with MOVE at 92.4, +7.5%, is the trade the equity rally is ignoring until the bond market reopens.

good.text: Volatility collapsed: VIX -10.1% to 17.49, VIX3M -6.8% to 19.24, term structure back down to 0.909 and SKEW -1.3%. The panic bid in protection is gone.
Credit confirmed the bounce rather than lagging it: HY OAS -8bp to 3.34, CCC -6bp, BBB -3bp, IG -2bp, HYG/IEF +0.4% and turning up, loans (BKLN) at the 97th percentile of the year.
The AI complex got its first genuine upside catalyst in two weeks — NDX +2.3% and turning up, TSM +2.0%, AVGO +3.9%, AMD +1.3% — and Asia followed: TAIEX +2.9%, KOSPI +2.5%, Nikkei +1.5%.
Breadth and the domestic cyclical side keep working: RSP/SPY z=3.75, Russell +0.9%, Transports +1.2%, XLF +6.5% on the month with relative strength +10.6%, KRE +5.9%.

No recession in the macro: claims 189k at the 0th percentile of the year, unemployment 4.1%, JOLTS 7,523 and +4.6%, industrial production and capacity utilization both at the 100th percentile. Growth pulse +11.
India is the cleanest trend in the dataset: Sensex +11.9% on the month at z=2.87, INDA +12.4% with acceleration +2.86, and the rupee firming (USDINR -2.9% on the month, z=-2.85).

bad.text: The dollar is the squeeze that won't stop: DXY 102.83 at the 100th percentile, EURUSD 1.1098 at the 0th, USDCHF +0.9%, USDCAD at the 96th. Dollar composite -22.
Brazil is a funding accident in progress: USDBRL +1.3% to 5.5827 at z=3.44 with acceleration +2.79, EWZ -26.2% on the month with acceleration -3.47, Bovespa z=-3.45.

Rates never validated the rally — the market was shut. As of the 9th-10th: 2y 4.56 (+5bp), 10y 4.88, 30y 5.26, 10y real 2.66 and 19% above its 200-day, 2s10s 25bp at the 9th percentile, MOVE +7.5% to 92.4.
Precious metals broke: gold 4,004 at the 7th percentile and 10.9% below its 200-day, silver at the 4th, GDX -5.4%, GDXJ -6.0%, NEM -4.2% — the miner squeeze unwound in one session.
The AI power chain sat out the rebound entirely: GEV -3.9%, CEG -3.0%, NLR -3.6%, URA -3.5%, with VST -18.8%, ETN -17.3% and GRID -11.9% on the month. Chips rallied, electrons did not.

Spreads are still wider on the month despite today's tightening and the speculative tail is dead: CCC +58bp, HY +23bp, BBB z=1.34; ARKK -14.0% and IPO -12.4% on the month; BTC 73,574 (-11.5%), COIN at the 0th percentile.

trades.name: Unwind the unwind: high beta vs low vol
trades.line: Long SPHB / short SPLV — fade a 3-sigma factor dislocation
trades.expr: Buy SPHB, sell SPLV, dollar-neutral 1:1. Scale in over two days; size so a 7% adverse move on the pair is tolerable.
trades.thesis: The drawdown was a positioning event, not a macro event. High-beta/low-vol fell 19.9% in a month to z=-3.09 while SPLV printed z=2.33 and RSP/SPY z=3.75 — both tails are three sigma simultaneously. With claims at 189k and JOLTS +4.6%, there is no earnings recession to justify permanently repricing beta into defensives.
trades.trigger: VIX -10.1% to 17.49 with VIX3M -6.8% and HY OAS -8bp: the vol and credit inputs that drove the defensive bid both reversed today, and NDX closed +2.3% while SPLV-type names (MCD z=3.83, HD z=2.84) are stretched to 3-sigma one-month moves.
trades.stop: VIX back above 22 with HY OAS retaking 3.60, or the pair down 7% — that says it is a de-rating, not a rotation.
trades.target: Half the one-month gap closed: SPHB/SPLV back toward -9% off its lows, roughly +10% on the pair.

trades.name: Semis washout bounce via SMH and Taiwan
trades.line: Long SMH + EWT after a -21% month and an AI re-rate
trades.expr: Buy SMH outright (2/3) plus EWT (1/3). For a defined-risk version, Dec/Jan SMH call spreads 5-10% out of the money funded by selling downside you would own.
trades.thesis: Semis took the entire drawdown: SOXX -21.4% and SMH -19.8% on the month, SMH/SPY z=-2.74 at the 36th percentile, SMH 7.4% below its 200-day. A single credible datapoint on AI capex flipped the tape; the group is the highest-beta way to express a reversal with the sell-side already de-rated.
trades.trigger: NDX +2.3%, TSM +2.0%, AVGO +3.9%, AMD +1.3% and TAIEX +2.9% overnight (+5.8% on the week), with EWT turning up and only 0.6% above its 200-day — the Asian supply chain is confirming, not fading, the US move.
trades.stop: SMH takes out last week's low or the basket is -8%; NVDA failing to hold 160 after today's rebound also kills it.
trades.target: +12%: SMH back to its 200-day, SMH/SPY retracing to the -8% relative level.

trades.name: Short the AI electron chain
trades.line: Short GEV / VST / NLR — power didn't join the chip bounce
trades.expr: Equal-weight short basket GEV, VST, NLR. Pair against the SMH long above if you want the net exposure flat.
trades.thesis: The AI trade is bifurcating. Chips are a cyclical with a catalyst; the power/grid complex was an infinite-duration story priced on a 2030 capex curve, and it is de-rating independently — GEV -20.6%, VST -18.8%, ETN -17.3%, GRID -11.9% on the month with GRID 10.5% below its 200-day and NLR 26% below.
trades.trigger: On a day SPX rose 1.3% and NDX 2.3%, GEV fell 3.9%, CEG 3.0%, NLR 3.6%, URA 3.5% and REMX 3.5%. Non-participation in a rip is the cleanest short signal in the digest.
trades.stop: Basket +9%, or GEV reclaiming its 200-day (it is 15.9% below) on utility/grid order news; XLU turning back up from its rolling_over state.
trades.target: -12% on the basket, with NLR and VST making new 52-week lows (currently 8th and 25th percentile).

trades.name: LatAm divergence: short Brazil, long Mexico
trades.line: Short EWZ / long EWW as USDBRL accelerates to z=3.4
trades.expr: Short EWZ, long EWW, 1:1 dollars. Equivalent in FX: long USDBRL vs short USDMXN.
trades.thesis: Brazil has moved from wobble to dislocation and the currency is leading: USDBRL +12.0% in a month, z=3.44, acceleration +2.79 at the 99th percentile, while the equity market is down 17.7% in local terms and 26.2% in dollars. Mexico is the mirror — IPC at the 100th percentile of its year, +7.9% on the month, EWW turning up, USDMXN quiet at +0.1%.
trades.trigger: USDBRL +1.3% again today while DXY printed the 100th percentile; EWZ acceleration -3.47 is the most negative in the dataset.
trades.stop: USDBRL back below 5.35 (a credible policy/intervention response) or the pair -8%.
trades.target: +10% on the pair over the horizon; EWZ to the 5th percentile of its 52-week range.

trades.name: India over the EM index
trades.line: Long INDA / short EEM — the only EM with a bid currency
trades.expr: Long INDA, short EEM, 1:1. Take the pair, not outright INDA — EM beta is still broken.
trades.thesis: EM is not one asset today. EEM is -9.3% on the month at z=-1.96 with EEM/SPY at the 13th percentile, dragged by Korea (-21.5%) and Brazil (-26.2%). India is the opposite: Sensex +11.9% on the month at z=2.87, INDA +12.4% with acceleration +2.86, supported by the one EM currency actually appreciating against a 100th-percentile dollar.
trades.trigger: USDINR -2.9% on the month at z=-2.85 and rolling over, with INDA relative strength +16.6% over one month and turning up; Sensex added another 0.1% while EEM fell 0.8%.
trades.stop: USDINR back above 96 or the pair -6%; a broad EM squeeze-higher led by Korea/Taiwan would also neutralize it.
trades.target: +9% on the pair as INDA recovers its -4.3% YTD and EEM lags.

trades.name: Short the long end into a hot-inflation reopen
trades.line: Short TLT: 30y 5.26, breakevens at the 6th percentile
trades.expr: Short TLT outright, or buy Dec/Jan TLT puts 3-5% out of the money. Cash equivalent: short 30y futures.
trades.thesis: Ten-year breakevens at 2.20 (6th percentile) and five-year at 2.25 while core CPI is turning up at z=0.93 with the index at the 100th percentile and the inflation composite rebounding to +27 from +13. Yields fell 34-36bp across 5s-30s over the month on growth fear; equities have now unwound that fear and the bond market has not repriced.
trades.trigger: The Treasury market was closed for the holiday while SPX rallied 1.3% and VIX fell 10.1%; the last prints show the front end backing up (2y +5bp, 3m +5bp) and MOVE +7.5% to 92.4 — the reopen is the catalyst.
trades.stop: TLT +4% (10y through 4.60), or a genuine growth crack — claims above 230k or HY OAS back over 3.75.

trades.name: Silver over gold on a stretched ratio
trades.line: Long silver / short gold: ratio 77.4 at the 88th percentile
trades.expr: Long SI futures / short GC futures, equal notional; ETF version long SLV short GLD. Small size — this is a 3-week mean-reversion trade, not a view on the metals complex.
trades.thesis: The precious unwind has been indiscriminate but lopsided: gold/silver +11.1% in a month to 77.4 at z=1.63 and the 88th percentile, with silver 25.5% below its 200-day at the 4th percentile of its year versus gold 10.9% below at the 7th. When the real-rate squeeze pauses, the beta leg snaps back first.
trades.trigger: Silver +1.2% today while gold fell 0.6%; the ratio turned down 1.8% in a single session after a one-way month, and copper +0.6% with copper/gold +1.3% says industrial demand is not the problem.
trades.stop: Ratio back above 82, or the pair -10%; a further leg of dollar strength (DXY through 104) would hit silver harder.
trades.target: Ratio back to 70, roughly +10% on the pair.
